Verifier, JIT backend, map lifecycle and full program lifecycle beyond execution wrappers.

findings.text: Builders provide sign-extending register moves for 64-bit and 32-bit ALU domains. Each accepts destination, source and offset inputs, uses register-source move semantics, carries the offset, and fixes the immediate to zero, differing only in ALU width.

Zero-extension idiom uses a 32-bit register-source move where destination and source select the same register, offset is cleared and immediate is one. A predicate recognizes this idiom by width, move kind, source kind and immediate value.

A predicate identifies user address-space cast markers as 64-bit register moves carrying a dedicated address-space offset tag together with a fixed large immediate. Only that combination of class, offset tag and immediate qualifies.

Wide immediate loads occupy two instruction slots to carry 64 bits. The first slot holds load semantics with destination and source selectors and the low half, the second slot is reserved with cleared fields holding the high half. A map variant reuses the raw form with a pseudo map descriptor source tag, and a simplified form defaults the source selector to zero.

Raw move builders cover 64-bit and 32-bit widths with caller-chosen source kind. They accept destination, source and immediate inputs, clear the offset, and encode move semantics in the selected width.

Load builders distinguish absolute packet loads, indirect packet loads with a source register, memory loads with base plus offset, and sign-extending memory loads. Size is caller-selected; absolute forms clear registers while indirect and memory forms wire source or base and destination as appropriate, with immediates or offsets per mode.

Store builders cover register-to-memory, immediate-to-memory and atomic memory operations. Register and immediate stores clear the unused field and carry offset. Atomic form carries size, destination, source, offset and an operation selector in the immediate; an add-only shorthand fixes that selector to addition.

Atomic memory operations expose classification helpers. One reports true only for acquire-load and release-store selectors. Another additionally requires store-with-register class and atomic or probe-atomic mode. A third maps the selector to the register holding the observed value, using destination for acquire-load, return register for compare-exchange, source when fetch is indicated, otherwise a negative sentinel for no loaded value.
Mode extraction isolates a fixed upper-bit field of the operation code using mask value 224. It defines the ABI position of addressing mode bits.

Jump builders cover conditional and unconditional control flow for full and 32-bit domains. Register forms carry two registers and an offset with cleared immediate; immediate forms carry destination, immediate and offset with cleared source. Unconditional forms include a full-width offset jump and a 32-bit variant carrying its target in the immediate with cleared offset.

Call builders distinguish relative pseudo calls, direct helper calls computed as displacement from a call base, and kernel-function calls with offset plus immediate. Relative and kernel-function forms tag the source field with dedicated pseudo markers, while direct emission clears source and offset.
Miscellaneous builders provide a fully caller-specified instruction, a function exit with cleared registers offset and immediate, and a speculation-barrier store with cleared fields.
Legacy packet-filter helpers wrap classic statement and jump encodings into socket-filter records, accepting operation code with constant, or code with constant plus true and false targets.

Size helpers translate between byte counts and BPF width selectors for one, two, four and eight bytes, returning a negative error sentinel otherwise. Type and field variants enforce validity at build time. A load-store byte helper derives the width from an instruction and warns on invalid selectors.

Helper definition machinery generates a typed front declaration, a function-pointer type for type information, and a fixed five-register ABI entry that forwards to an always-inline implementation with argument casting and padding of unused slots. Variants support zero to five typed arguments plus a non-tracing single-argument form.

Context-access helpers express allowed byte ranges of a type member using member boundaries, including ranges spanning to a second member and pointer-sized variants whose width depends on configuration. A target-offset helper validates member size at build time, records it through an output, and yields the member offset.

Classic filter programs have compatible and kernel layouts. Both carry a 16-bit length. The compatible form pairs it with a compat pointer to filter records, while the kernel form pairs it with a native pointer.
JIT image alignment requirement is eight bytes.

Binary header pairs a 32-bit size with a variable image honoring the alignment. Program statistics group invocation count, total time and miss count with a synchronizer and carry sixteen-byte alignment. Timed goto state pairs a counter with a timestamp. Socket filter wrapper pairs a reference count with deferred-release linkage and a program pointer.

Program execution invokes a dispatcher over context plus cached instruction and function pointers under a non-migratable assumption. It consults an external statistics-enabled predicate and, when indicated, accounts count and duration via external per-CPU and clock facilities if program statistics storage is present. A thin wrapper selects the default dispatcher, and a pinned variant brackets the run with external migration-control operations.

Counter update framing has a lightweight configuration where begin, end and interrupt-state steps are inert, and a protected configuration where begin and end delegate to external preemption, sequencing and interrupt-state facilities with begin producing a token consumed by end. Accumulation itself is either direct or via external local accumulation, with increment as unit delta.

Parameter spill idioms are recognized by width, class, register and offset shape. Loads use the parameter register as source with positive eight-aligned offsets; stores use it as destination with negative eight-aligned offsets, distinguishing immediate versus register store classes.

Socket-buffer metadata overlays control storage with queueing control plus meta and end pointers. Next-hop parameters pair an address family with a union holding either an IPv4 address or an IPv6 address. A control-length alias equates scratch length with queueing private length.

Redirect state uses five single-bit flags in kernel flags occupying bits zero through four in listed order: one suppresses direct return handling, and four record one-time initialization of redirect info and of CPU, device and XSK flush lists.

Redirect info groups target index and value, map pointer, user flags, map identifier and type, next-hop parameters and kernel flags. Network context groups redirect info with three flush lists for CPU, device and XSK maps.

Network context follows install, use and clear phases on current task storage. Install fails when one is already present and otherwise clears kernel flags before publishing; clear detaches when present. Accessors lazily initialize redirect info and each flush list exactly once as tracked by kernel flags. Collection reports only initialized non-empty lists, honoring build configuration gates, and otherwise yields nulls.

Data-pointer computation derives metadata start and data end from head data adjusted by metadata length and head length, with a build assertion that the metadata overlay fits control storage. Head length is total length minus paged length; metadata length comes from shared-info state reached via the buffer end pointer.
Execution assumes the caller does not migrate CPUs across the run. One configuration delegates to an external check with source context when multiprocessing is enabled, the other is inert.

Several misuse risks apply. Wide immediates consume two slots and the trailing slot uses a reserved operation code, so slot counting must account for pairs. Atomic classification returning a negative sentinel must not be used as a register index. Lazy context accessors assume installed context and must not be called when absent. Flush-list collection may yield nulls that callers must handle. Image storage requires stated alignment and statistics require aligned grouping with external synchronization.
